metadata.title: Example Sensor Gateway System Security Plan (draft)

system-characteristics.description: The system gives the installation security operations center (SOC) a near-real-time picture of perimeter intrusion and environmental conditions (temperature, flooding, power loss) at remote sites . It senses and forwards only: it makes no decisions and actuates nothing, and operators act on alarms through separate systems .

information-types.title: Perimeter and environmental sensor telemetry and alarms
information-types.description: Intrusion, door, temperature, water and power readings and alarms with site and sensor identifiers, collected from the field sensor network and forwarded to IODS.

availability-impact.adjustment-justification: An outage removes sensing at one site; the SOC compensates with guard patrols for several days, so the provisional low value is kept.

information-types.title: ESG configuration and security management data
information-types.description: Device configuration, host firewall rules, account records and cryptographic keys of the gateway.

confidentiality-impact.adjustment-justification: The data includes private keys and firewall rules whose disclosure would let an attacker impersonate a gateway or map the permitted paths into the enclave.

information-types.title: ESG audit records
information-types.description: Sign-in, account change, privilege use, configuration change and update events.

authorization-boundary.description: The boundary holds the gateway appliance at each site with its operating system, sensor collector, admin web console and local buffer database, plus the field sensor nodes paired with it; all units share one configuration baseline and are authorized as one system. The edge is the installation network switch port on the gateway uplink. IODS, the Installation ICAM Service, the Installation Network Enclave and the Installation CSSP are outside the boundary and separately authorized.

network-architecture.description: The gateway uplink sits on the ESG VLAN of the installation enclave and permits only outbound TLS 1.3 to IODS, outbound syslog over TLS to the CSSP SIEM, TLS to the identity service and inbound HTTPS to the console from the installation management VLAN; the host firewall denies all other traffic and the enclave firewall enforces the same flows. The maintenance port is disabled unless enabled by the shelter key switch, serves only the console on a link-local address and does not route to the uplink. Sensor nodes connect only to their paired gateway over the encrypted field radio and have no IP connectivity.

data-flow.description: DF-1 sensor readings and alarms from nodes to the collector over the paired, encrypted radio; DF-2 collector to the local buffer on the encrypted data partition; DF-3 collector to IODS over TLS 1.3 with mutual certificate authentication; DF-4 audit records from the gateway to the CSSP SIEM over syslog TLS; DF-5 administrator workstation to the console over HTTPS; DF-6 console to the identity service over TLS with signed assertions; DF-7 technician laptop to the console over HTTPS on the maintenance port with local sign-in.

authorized-privileges.title: Emergency administration
functions-performed: restore console access when the identity service is unavailable

components.title: Example Sensor Gateway
components.description: The system gives the installation security operations center (SOC) a near-real-time picture of perimeter intrusion and environmental conditions (temperature, flooding, power loss) at remote sites . components.title: ESG gateway appliance
components.description: Ruggedized fanless appliance with uplink and maintenance Ethernet ports and a field radio module (INV-001, INV-006)

components.title: Gateway operating system
components.description: Hardened Linux-based OS image with host firewall and local audit daemon (INV-002)

components.title: Sensor collector service
components.description: Receives and validates sensor messages, writes them to the buffer and forwards them to IODS (INV-003)

components.title: Admin web console
components.description: HTTPS console for configuration, accounts, diagnostics and update upload (INV-004)

components.title: Local buffer database
components.description: Embedded database holding up to 7 days of telemetry while IODS is unreachable (INV-005)

components.title: Field sensor network
components.description: Up to 40 battery-powered sensor nodes per site and their firmware (INV-007, INV-008)

components.title: Installation Operations Data Service
components.description: Receives ESG telemetry (IC-1) under an interconnection agreement; separately authorized

components.title: Installation ICAM Service
components.description: Installation identity provider giving DoD PKI sign-in for remote ESG administrators and auditors (IC-2); covered by the enclave authorization

components.title: Installation Network Enclave
components.description: Enclave firewall, intrusion detection and network access control in front of every ESG; separately authorized

components.title: Installation Cybersecurity Service Provider
components.description: SIEM log collection and correlation, monitoring and incident response support; separately authorized

inventory-items.description: Gateway appliance: ruggedized fanless edge appliance with uplink and maintenance Ethernet ports and a field radio module
Hardened Linux-based gateway OS image with host firewall, local audit daemon and nightly configuration check
Sensor collector service: receives and validates sensor messages, buffers them and forwards them to IODS
Admin web console (HTTPS) for configuration, accounts, diagnostics and update upload
Embedded local buffer database holding up to 7 days of telemetry while IODS is unreachable
Firmware of the gateway's field radio module
Battery-powered field sensor node (up to 40 per site) with no IP connectivity
Firmware of the field sensor nodes

control-implementation.description: Planned and implemented controls for baseline CNSSI1253-M-M-L-SUBSET-6.

by-components.description: Allowed account types are identity-service accounts for remote administrators and auditors (console roles admin and auditor, mapped from group claims), one sealed break-glass account (esgadmin) whose use is logged and reported, and the shared local field-technician account fieldtech; no other account type is permitted. The ISSO is the account manager and approves every ESG access request; the Installation ICAM Service account workflow then creates the account and its group claim, and removing the claim removes access. CMP-WEBUI enforces the role mapping, CMP-GW-OS forwards sign-in and account-change events to the SIEM so account use is monitored, and the ISSO reviews the console account list against the access request records quarterly (last record 2026-09-12). Missing: fieldtech is a shared account used by ten technicians, its password changes every 90 days rather than when a technician leaves the team, and its use cannot be attributed to an individual. Plan: per-technician local accounts with smart-card login in release 2.3, planned for 2027-03.

CMP-GW-OS (audit daemon), CMP-COLLECTOR and CMP-WEBUI log sign-in success and failure, account changes, privilege use, configuration changes, update installation, service start and stop, and radio pairing events. The event list was coordinated and agreed with the Installation CSSP on 2026-05-20 as the set an incident investigation needs, and the ISSO and the CSSP review and update it annually. Events are forwarded over TLS to the CSSP SIEM within one minute and held locally for 30 days; the CSSP correlates them and the ISSO reviews the ESG report weekly. Shared responsibility: the CSSP provides collection and correlation, ESG generates and forwards the events. Events from the shared fieldtech account are logged but name the account, not a person (tracked under ac-2).

by-components.description: Configuration settings for CMP-GW-OS, CMP-COLLECTOR, CMP-WEBUI and CMP-STORE are established from the DISA SRGs and STIGs applicable to each component (General Purpose OS SRG and the application and web server guidance) and implemented in one signed OS image that the developer's build pipeline hardens for every unit. The pipeline records each deviation; the RSSPO configuration control board approves deviations, which are listed in the STIG summary. A nightly configuration check on every unit reports drift from the approved baseline to the SIEM, and every baseline change goes through the configuration control board. The 2026-09-30 scan found the approved baseline on all 12 units with only the approved deviations.

In place: remote administrators and auditors authenticate to CMP-WEBUI with their DoD PKI smart card at the Installation ICAM Service; the console federates to the service and maps the approved group claim to the admin or auditor role, so each remote session and the processes acting in it are associated with one named person. Users without an approved claim are refused (DT-2). The sealed break-glass account esgadmin is used by one named person per use, and each use is logged and reported to the ISSO. The console locks local accounts for 30 minutes after five failed sign-ins and locks sessions after 15 minutes idle. Shared responsibility: the Installation ICAM Service provides PKI authentication; ESG provides the federation, role mapping and session handling. Missing: on the maintenance port the ten field technicians sign in with the shared local fieldtech password account, so their sessions are not uniquely identified and cannot be associated with an individual. Plan: release 2.3 (planned 2027-03) replaces fieldtech with per-technician local accounts with smart-card login that work without a path to the identity service.

a. The host firewall in CMP-GW-OS on each CMP-GW-HW appliance monitors and controls traffic at the uplink and maintenance ports, denying by default and permitting only outbound TLS 1.3 to IODS, outbound syslog over TLS to the CSSP, and inbound HTTPS to the console from the installation management VLAN; the maintenance port is disabled until the shelter key switch enables it, serves only a link-local console and never routes to the uplink, and sensor nodes have no IP path. b. ESG has no publicly accessible components. c. ESG connects to external systems only through the site switch behind the Installation Network Enclave, whose firewall, intrusion detection and network access control enforce the same permitted flows at the enclave edge. Shared responsibility: the enclave provides edge boundary protection; ESG provides the host firewall and port separation. DT-2 port scans from both ports found only the documented ports and no routing between them.

values: 30 days from release of the update bundle

by-components.description: In place: a. the developer tracks flaws in CMP-GW-OS, CMP-COLLECTOR, CMP-WEBUI and CMP-STORE and corrects them in a signed monthly update bundle; vulnerability scans report flaws on fielded units to the ISSO. b. Each bundle is built by the hardened-image pipeline and tested on the developer's reference units before release, and units verify the bundle signature before installing it. d. Each bundle changes the approved baseline and goes through the RSSPO configuration control board. Missing: c. fielded units receive bundles only at the quarterly site visit, so security-relevant updates are not installed within 30 days from release of the update bundle; at the 2026-09-30 scan two of 12 units (esg-north-01, esg-ridge-01) ran a 63-day-old bundle with 4 high and 9 medium vulnerabilities fixed in later bundles. Plan: release 2.2 (planned 2026-12) adds remote update over the uplink so bundles are installed within the 30-day period.
